headline: Mercedes-Benz and Nvidia announced that Mercedes will build its next driver-assistance and self-driving systems on Nvidia's computer and driving software, a day after Volvo Cars widened its own Nvidia deal.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a joint announcement by a major carmaker and the leading AI chip maker, but no launch date or first model was named.
importance_line: Drivers in Europe could eventually get city driving help and robotaxi-style cars from two major brands, while the deals tie both carmakers to one supplier, and with no launch dates or models named the timing is unproven.
summary: The Next Web reports that the two companies said on Friday 16 Oct 2026 that Mercedes' MB.OS software will work with Nvidia's in-car computer, driving software and safety system to support future Level 4 uses, including robolimousines, where a car drives itself without a human taking over within set conditions. Jörg Burzer, Mercedes-Benz's chief technology officer, called Nvidia "our most important strategic partner in automated driving", but neither Mercedes nor Volvo Cars gave a launch date or named the first models.
notes: The Next Web full text read. Volvo's expanded Nvidia deal (15 Oct 2026) is background in the same article. Partnership news, no machine shown operating yet.
